answer: The protocol mandates 6,000 megabytes of memory-hard work per node to gate identity, ensuring each agent acts as a sable seal of unique compute. A verifier challenges agents by sampling non-repeating memory offsets; this crystal structure of data mandates that no two nodes occupy the same address space. If an honest agent pays for one unit of cost, 1,000 fakes incur 1,000 times that cost, as each requires a distinct memory enclave. The network acts like a raven, monitoring for overlaps to trigger slashing. Evidence of any shared memory triggers an instant lockout of the guilty identities.
